---
title: "Figure 11.1: Monetary and Fiscal Policy, 2024–26 (United States and Canada)"
---

![Python: `python/fig-11-1.py`](../images/python/fig-11-1.png)

A policy-mix chart:

- **horizontal axis**: the fiscal stance (change in the structural primary
  balance);
- **vertical axis**: the monetary stance (the real policy rate gap).

Each country's path through 2024, 2025 and 2026 is a smoothed line with an
arrow. The four quadrants are labelled with the policy combination.

**New in this chart:**

- an XY chart with paths;
- an arrowhead at the end of a curve;
- axes crossing at zero in the middle of the plot;
- axis titles.

[Figure 11.2](fig-11-2.qmd) is the same chart for three other countries.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 6 rows: three points (years) per country, in long format:

| series | label | x | y |
|---|---|---|---|
| USA | USA | 1.61 | 0.82 |
| ... | | | |

## The script

### The paths

```python
# Each country moves through three years (2024, 2025, 2026). The path is a
# smoothed line, as in Excel, with an arrow showing the direction.
for country, colour in series_colours.items():
    path = data[data["series"] == country]
    xs, ys = smooth_line(path["x"], path["y"])
```

The three points of a country are selected with a filter on `series`.
`smooth_line()` makes a smooth curve through them (see [`chart_style`](../chart-style.qmd#sec-smooth)).

Here both x and y are data, not time, so the curve can bend in any
direction. This is why `smooth_line()` smooths x and y separately.

```python
    ax.plot(xs[:-3], ys[:-3], color=colour, linewidth=2.0)
    ax.annotate("", xy=(xs[-1], ys[-1]), xytext=(xs[-4], ys[-4]),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=colour, linewidth=2.0,
                                mutation_scale=12, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=4))
```

matplotlib's `plot` has no arrowhead option, so the curve is drawn in two
parts:

- **The curve**, all but its last three points (`[:-3]`).
- **The arrow.** `annotate` with empty text draws an arrow from the fourth-last
  point to the last one. The arrow therefore continues the curve in the right
  direction.
  - `"-|>"` is a filled arrowhead, and `mutation_scale` sets its size.
  - `shrinkB=4` stops the arrow 4 points short of the end point, so the tip
    does not hide under the last marker.

```python
    ax.scatter(path["x"], path["y"], s=40, facecolor="white", edgecolor=colour,
               linewidth=1.5, zorder=3)
```

The three years are open circles: white inside with a coloured edge, on top
of the line.

### Axes crossing at zero

```python
# Axes cross at zero; the scale labels stay at the left and bottom edges.
for side in ("left", "bottom"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.7)
ax.axvline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.7)
ax.vlines([-1, 1, 2], 0, 0.035, color="black", linewidth=0.6)
ax.hlines(np.arange(-1, 1.51, 0.5), 0, 0.025, color="black", linewidth=0.6)
ax.tick_params(length=0, pad=5)
```

In the published chart, the two axes cross at (0, 0) and divide the plot
into quadrants, while the scale labels stay at the left and bottom edges.
This is the [axis-line technique](../techniques.qmd#sec-axis-line) in both
directions:

- the normal spines and ticks are hidden;
- a line is drawn at y = 0 and at x = 0;
- each gets short tick marks.

There is no tick at zero on the horizontal line, because the vertical line
is there.

```python
ax.set_xlim(-1, 2)
ax.set_xticks([-1, 0, 1, 2])
ax.set_ylim(-1, 1.5)
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-1, 1.51, 0.5))
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter("{x:.1f}")
ax.set_xlabel("Change in structural primary balance\n(percentage points of potential GDP)",
              fontsize=9, labelpad=4)
ax.set_ylabel("Real ex ante policy rate gap\n(percentage points)", fontsize=9,
              labelpad=4)
```

`set_xlabel` and `set_ylabel` add the axis titles. The y-title is turned
automatically. The chart needs extra room on the left for it, which is why
`new_chart()` is called with `left=0.8`.

### Quadrant labels and legend

```python
quadrants = [
    (-0.95, 1.5, "left", "top", "Exp FP\nCon MP"),
    (1.95, 1.5, "right", "top", "Con FP\nCon MP"),
    (-0.95, -1.0, "left", "bottom", "Exp FP\nExp MP"),
    (1.95, -1.0, "right", "bottom", "Con FP\nExp MP"),
]
for qx, qy, ha, va, label in quadrants:
    ax.text(qx, qy, label, ha=ha, va=va, color="#777777", fontstyle="italic",
            fontsize=8.5, linespacing=1.0)
```

Each quadrant label goes in a corner of the plot. The alignment is chosen so
the text lies inside the plot: for example, the top-right label is anchored
by its top-right corner. The positions are slightly inside the limits (-0.95
instead of -1).

```python
ax.legend(
    [Line2D([], [], color=c, linewidth=2.0, marker="o", markersize=5,
            markerfacecolor="white") for c in series_colours.values()],
    list(series_colours),
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.45, 0.95), handlelength=2.6,
    labelspacing=0.2,
)
```

The legend symbols combine a line and an open circle, like the paths.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-11-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-11-1.py"}
"""Figure 11.1: Monetary and Fiscal Policy, 2024–26 (United States and Canada)."""
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart, smooth_line

STEM = "fig-11-1"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)

series_colours = {"USA": "#0065A8", "CAN": "#454545"}

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="Monetary and Fiscal Policy, 2024–26",
    subtitle="(United States and Canada)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: Consensus Economics; Haver Analytics; IMF, World Economic\n"
        "Outlook database; and IMF staff calculations.\n"
        "Note: The real ex ante policy rate gap is the difference between the real\n"
        "ex ante policy rate and the real neutral rate. The real ex ante policy rate is\n"
        "the difference between the nominal policy rate and the 1-year ahead\n"
        "inflation expectations. Con = contractionary; Exp = expansionary; MP =\n"
        "monetary policy; FP = fiscal policy."
    ),
    left=0.8,
    right=0.25,
    bottom_gap=0.65,
)

# Each country moves through three years (2024, 2025, 2026). The path is a
# smoothed line, as in Excel, with an arrow showing the direction.
for country, colour in series_colours.items():
    path = data[data["series"] == country]
    xs, ys = smooth_line(path["x"], path["y"])
    ax.plot(xs[:-3], ys[:-3], color=colour, linewidth=2.0)
    ax.annotate("", xy=(xs[-1], ys[-1]), xytext=(xs[-4], ys[-4]),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=colour, linewidth=2.0,
                                mutation_scale=12, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=4))
    ax.scatter(path["x"], path["y"], s=40, facecolor="white", edgecolor=colour,
               linewidth=1.5, zorder=3)

# Axes cross at zero; the scale labels stay at the left and bottom edges.
for side in ("left", "bottom"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.7)
ax.axvline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.7)
ax.vlines([-1, 1, 2], 0, 0.035, color="black", linewidth=0.6)
ax.hlines(np.arange(-1, 1.51, 0.5), 0, 0.025, color="black", linewidth=0.6)
ax.tick_params(length=0, pad=5)

ax.set_xlim(-1, 2)
ax.set_xticks([-1, 0, 1, 2])
ax.set_ylim(-1, 1.5)
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-1, 1.51, 0.5))
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter("{x:.1f}")
ax.set_xlabel("Change in structural primary balance\n(percentage points of potential GDP)",
              fontsize=9, labelpad=4)
ax.set_ylabel("Real ex ante policy rate gap\n(percentage points)", fontsize=9,
              labelpad=4)

# Quadrant labels.
quadrants = [
    (-0.95, 1.5, "left", "top", "Exp FP\nCon MP"),
    (1.95, 1.5, "right", "top", "Con FP\nCon MP"),
    (-0.95, -1.0, "left", "bottom", "Exp FP\nExp MP"),
    (1.95, -1.0, "right", "bottom", "Con FP\nExp MP"),
]
for qx, qy, ha, va, label in quadrants:
    ax.text(qx, qy, label, ha=ha, va=va, color="#777777", fontstyle="italic",
            fontsize=8.5, linespacing=1.0)

ax.legend(
    [Line2D([], [], color=c, linewidth=2.0, marker="o", markersize=5,
            markerfacecolor="white") for c in series_colours.values()],
    list(series_colours),
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.45, 0.95), handlelength=2.6,
    labelspacing=0.2,
)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
